title: test-0009-SCI-BIO-FORESTS
passage: Deep within the Western Ghats, forest rangers are observing a remarkable recovery in a protected patch of woodland. Unlike a simple collection of trees, this forest functions as a complex, interconnected system where every organism plays a vital role. On the forest floor, tiny organisms act as decomposers, breaking down fallen leaves and dead matter into dark, nutrient-rich humus that enriches the soil. This process is not a disappearance into nothingness, but a recycling of essential nutrients back into the earth. Nearby, a group of monkeys feeds on wild figs, inadvertently dropping seeds across the forest floor, which helps new trees grow and ensures the forest expands. The trees themselves act as a giant sponge, releasing water vapor through transpiration, which increases humidity and encourages local rainfall. Because of this, the forest acts as a natural water regulator. Furthermore, the dense canopy is not a solid ceiling; it is a layered structure that allows light to filter through, supporting diverse life forms below. Even the plants here respire, taking in oxygen and releasing carbon dioxide at night, just as they produce oxygen during the day. This dynamic balance ensures that the forest remains a living entity, constantly renewing itself while providing resources like fallen branches that can be harvested without destroying the entire ecosystem.
summary: On the forest floor, tiny organisms break down leaves and dead matter into dark, nutrient-rich soil. Nearby, a group of monkeys eats wild figs. They drop the seeds, which helps new trees grow and makes the forest grow.
